problem: Existing edge resource management for multi-robot systems optimizes sensing coverage, communication rate or computation, ignoring that different robots contribute unequally to the aggregated memory that EQA answers depend on. Task-oriented communication needs closed-set objectives, while EQA questions are open-set and unknown at memory-collection time.
motivation: In multi-agent EQA the server merges robots' memories to answer later queries, so accuracy depends on memory quality rather than throughput or coverage. Although individual questions are unpredictable, question templates are finite, so questions can be generated from a robot's own memory and used to test the server's current memory, which gives a proxy for the value of that robot's data.
key_idea: Estimate each robot's memory novelty with a generative adversarial exam (LLM-generated questions from pilot data, tested against the server's existing memory), turn the scores into a quality-of-memory objective, and allocate transmit power to maximize it.
insight: Table I shows the novelty score (1-GAE_k) correlates with the EQA accuracy gain from adding robot k's memory (GAE 0.27 gives 70%, GAE 0.79 gives 39%), whereas BERT similarity scores are nearly indistinguishable across robots. Baselines that maximize rate (MaxRate) or coverage (MaxCov) do worse on accuracy, so communication and sensing are not always beneficial to memorization.
method: GAE (generative adversarial exam): each robot uploads a small pilot sample, the server captions it with a VLM, an LLM generates L_k QA pairs per robot, and the server's pre-collection memory M0 is tested on them; the score GAE_k is M0's answer accuracy, so low GAE means novel memory.

QoM model: expected accuracy gain of robot k is (1-GAE_k)*F_k(p)/sum|D_k|, where F_k is the number of frames uploaded under the rate (Shannon rate with interference, MRC). QoM(p) = sum_k min[Delta Psi_k, Theta_k(p)], a saturating sum, assuming each uploaded chunk contributes independently.

Overhead analysis: pilot upload is small because only tens of images are sampled, and exam latency is small because ReMEmbR-style iterative retrieval answers each QA in seconds and QAs run in parallel; the transmission time becomes T minus the GAE overhead.

Successive convex approximation: a concave lower-bound surrogate of the nonconvex rate term (Proposition 1) is solved iteratively with convex solvers such as Mosek, converging to stationary points; complexity is O(J K^3.5).

Noise-limited closed form: with interference negligible, the optimum is a GAE-augmented capped water-filling p_k = min[beta_k, [nu(1-GAE_k)T~B/(Z_k sum|D|) - sigma^2/H_k]^+] with saturation power beta_k and nu found by bisection; robots with GAE_k = 1 get zero power.
Memory pipeline: Qwen3-VL-8B captions images, mxbai-embed-large-v1 embeds them, and Milvus stores (time, pose, embedding); Qwen3-8B does iterative-retrieval EQA.

setting.backbone: Qwen3-VL-8B (captioning, frozen), mxbai-embed-large-v1 (embedding), Qwen3-8B (EQA/exam LLM, frozen); power allocation by convex optimization / water-filling
setting.observation: drone RGB camera frames with timestamp and 6-DoF pose (500 m inspection path, 1050 frames/drone)
setting.action_space: continuous per-robot transmit power allocation (no navigation actions)
setting.privileged: none at test time; ground-truth answers used only for evaluation (10 random objects, 30 questions per run)

numbers.eval_set_note: averaged over 50 random simulation runs; P_sum=200 mW, 30 questions per realization
numbers.extra: multi-agent memory aggregation; 5 of 10 drones form initial memory M0; T=10 min, B=10 MHz

numbers_note: Custom CARLA benchmark, not a standard navigation benchmark; sweeps over P_sum are given only in figures. Table I (K=5) lists per-robot GAE and accuracy but not a method result.
results: MCPA reaches 95.35% EQA accuracy and QoM 0.21, beating the best baseline MaxCov (86.09%, 0.19) and standalone Remember (41.0%). MaxRate has the highest sum-rate (59.04 Mbps) but only 61.69% accuracy, and MCPA is best in accuracy and QoM across all P_sum from 100 to 300 mW.
limitations: Evaluated only in one CARLA town with simple object-existence, location and which-drone questions and small 8B models; no real-robot or other-domain validation.
QoM assumes independent, additive memory contributions and perfect self-answering of a robot's own exam, and the closed form holds only in the noise-limited regime.
Static channels and a single time budget; battery lifetime and time-varying channels are left to future work.
